items.actClause:
AN ACT to amend the energy law, in relation to the purchase of fuel economy,
electric and hybrid passenger vehicles by the office of general services
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S2838

SPONSOR: PARKER
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the energy law, in relation to the purchase of fuel
economy, electric and hybrid passenger vehicles by the office of general
services

 
PURPOSE:

This legislation direct the Office of General Services to purchase elec-
tric vehicles for use in the state fleet of passenger vehicles.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1 - Amends Section 5-108 of the energy law to require the
commissioner to purchase battery, electric, plug-in hybrid, or zero
emissions vehicles by January 1, 2023. Additionally, requires the
commissioner to set targets for the acquisition of battery, electric,
plug-in and zero emissions vehicles. By 2031, all passenger vehicles in
the state shall be zero emissions vehicles.

Section 2 - Effective Immediately.

 
EXISTING LAW:

Under the current law, passenger vehicles purchased by the state must
meet certain miles per gallon standards.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

The transportation sector accounts for about 30% of the greenhouse gas
emissions in the nation. This proposal seeks to leverage the state's
purchasing power to increase the number of low emission and zero emis-
sion vehicles, therefore reducing the state's transportation sector
emissions. Additionally, the purchase of these vehicles will spur the
construction of the necessary infrastructure to power these vehicles
benefitting both the state and citizens seeking to purchase electric
vehicles but hesitant to do so because of range anxiety.

 
LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

2019/20 S5439A - AMEND AND RECOMMIT TO ENERGY AND TELECOMMUNICATIONS
PRINT NUMBER 5439A

2019: S.5439 - Passed Senate

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

To be determined.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This legislation shall take effect immediately.

A.actClause:
AN ACT to amend the executive law, in relation to the purchase or lease of
zero emission vehicles for state-owned vehicle fleets
A.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S2838A

SPONSOR: PARKER
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the executive law, in relation to the purchase or lease
of zero emission vehicles for state-owned vehicle fleets

 
PURPOSE:

This legislation direct the Office of General Services to purchase or
lease zero emission vehicles for use in state-owned vehicle fleets.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1 - Amends Section 201-a of the executive law to require the
Commissioner in consultation with the Department of Environmentalò
Conservation and New York State Energy Research and Development Authori-
ty, to develop a state fleet procurement plan for purchase or lease of
state agency vehicles; to ensure that 25% of state vehicles will be zero
emissions by December 21,2025; and 50% of state agency vehicles will be
zero emission no later than December 31, 2030. By January 1, 2030 all
passenger vehicles purchased by any state agency or public authority
shall be zero emission vehicles. This section also includes "zero emis-
sion vehicle" definition.

Section 2 - Effective Immediately.

 
EXISTING LAW:

Under the current law, passenger vehicles purchased by the state must
meet certain miles per gallon standards.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

The transportation sector accounts for about 36% of the greenhouse gas
emissions in the state and significant amounts of co-pollutant emissions
that impact the health and wellness of the state's citizens. This
proposal seeks to leverage the state's purchasing power to increase the
number of zero emission vehicles (ZEVs) on the road, therefore reducing
the state's transportation sector emissions.  Additionally, the purchase
of these vehicles will spur the development and deployment of light,
medium, and heavy-duty ZEVs and the construction of the necessary
infrastructure to power these vehicles.

 
LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

2019/20 S5439A - AMEND AND RECOMMIT TO ENERGY AND TELECOMMUNICATIONS
PRINT NUMBER 5439A

2019: S.5439 - Passed Senate

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

To be determined.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This legislation shall take effect immediately.

approvalMessage.text:
APPROVAL MEMORANDUM - No. 75 Chapter 789
 
       MEMORANDUM filed with Senate Bill Number 2838-C, entitled:
 
    "AN  ACT  to amend the executive law, in relation to the purchase or
        lease of zero emission vehicles for state-owned vehicle fleets"
 
    APPROVED
 
  This bill would require the  Office  of  General  Services  (OGS),  in
consultation with the Department of Environmental Conservation (DEC) and
the  New York State Energy Research and Development Authority (NYSERDA),
to prepare a state fleet procurement plan that ensures  that  the  state
fleet meets statutorily prescribed goals for zero emission vehicle (ZEV)
adoption.
 
  In  my  2022  State  of the State, I proposed that 100% of the State's
passenger fleet be electric by 2035 and 100% of the State's medium-  and
heavy-duty fleet be electric by 2040. In September 2022, I issued Execu-
tive  Order  22, which directs state agencies to create plans to achieve
these goals. Individual agencies are better suited to develop and imple-
ment these plans based on their need related to a specific fleet, rather
than OGS.
 
  I support investing in and electrifying the transportation  sector  to
help  New  York  achieve  its climate goals, and to achieve this, I have
reached an agreement with the Legislature to codify  certain  provisions
of my Executive Order.
 
  On  the  basis  of this agreement, I am pleased to sign this bill into
law.
 
  This bill is approved.                         (signed) KATHY HOCHUL
 
                                ______

summary: Directs the office of general services in consultation with the department of environmental conservation and the New York state energy research and development authority to prepare a state fleet procurement plan for the purchase or lease of state agency vehicles to ensure state agency vehicles will be zero emission vehicles over a certain period of time.
